items.q: The famous book of blessings (salawat) on our Beloved Prophet ﷺ written by Imam al-Jazuli ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ of Morocco.
The country of Imam al-Jazuli ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, author of Dala'il al-Khayrat.
The Swahili word, from Arabic, for a praise poem or song.
The Swahili name for the Blessed Mawlid and its recital, as in the festival of Lamu.
The island town in Kenya famous for its yearly Maulidi festival.
The founder of the Sokoto Caliphate who wrote many poems praising our Beloved Prophet ﷺ in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa.

items.q: The scholar and poet daughter of Shaykh 'Uthman ibn Fudi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, who wrote in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa.
The Senegalese scholar whose praise poems, called "khassaids", are chanted at Touba.
The holy city in Senegal founded by Shaykh Ahmadu Bamba ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Arabic word used in Mauritania and the Maghrib for chanting praise of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The Senegalese town of El Hadj Malick Sy ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, where a great Blessed Mawlid (Gamou) is held each year.
El Hadj Malick Sy's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ long poem on the Blessed Seerah is called "Khilas al-Dhahab", meaning this.

items.q: The Swahili poem "Utendi wa Hamziyya" translates this Arabic praise poem.
The city in Ethiopia, with its old walls, known as a centre of Islamic learning and devotional poetry.

items.q: The Ethiopian form of Islamic devotional poetry, often chanted in Amharic or Afaan Oromo.
The great Somali scholar of the Qadiri way, from Barawa, who wrote poems in Arabic and Somali.
The Moroccan art of chanting the Burdah and other praise poems is called "al-Sama' wal-Madih"; "madih" means this.
The city of Mali, with the Sankore Mosque, whose old manuscripts include many praise poems.
Imam al-Jazuli ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ is buried in this Moroccan city, as one of its "Seven Saints".
Imam al-Jazuli ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
The Sufi order linked with Imam al-Jazuli ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, a branch of the Shadhili way.
The Swahili "Utendi wa Hamziyya" is among the oldest dated works in this language.
The Sufi way founded by Shaykh Ahmadu Bamba ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The yearly gathering at Touba marking Shaykh Ahmadu Bamba's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ exile.
Shaykh 'Uthman ibn Fudi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
The city in Nigeria that was the capital of Shaykh 'Uthman ibn Fudi's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ state.
The Sufi way followed by El Hadj Malick Sy and Shaykh Ibrahim Niasse ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ما.
The country where Shaykh Ahmadu Bamba ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ was exiled by the French for seven years.
Nana Asma'u ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ا passed away in this year.
Shaykh Ahmadu Bamba ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
El Hadj Malick Sy ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
Shaykh Uways al-Barawi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
The Moroccan scholar who wrote "Mumti' al-Asma'", on al-Jazuli ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ and his followers.
Dala'il al-Khayrat is read in parts, one for each of these.
The Senegalese scholar and poet called "the Servant of the Messenger ﷺ" (Khadim al-Rasul).
Shaykh Ibrahim Niasse ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ passed away in this year.
The Mauritanian scholars who wrote and chanted praise poems taught in this kind of desert school.
The Hausa word for a poem, used for the religious poems of the Sokoto scholars.
The language of the Wolof-script (Wolofal) poems of Shaykh Ahmadu Bamba's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ followers, written in Arabic letters.
Writing an African language in Arabic letters, as in Hausa and Fulfulde poems, is called this.
Imam al-Jazuli's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ full name ends with this name of a Berber tribe of the Sus.
Muhammad al-Mahdi al-Fasi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ also wrote this commentary on Dala'il al-Khayrat.
The groups of women students Nana Asma'u ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ا taught across the Sokoto lands were called this.
The brother of Shaykh 'Uthman ibn Fudi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, a scholar-poet who wrote "Tazyin al-Waraqat".
The scholar of Ceuta whose book "al-Durr al-Munazzam" called for celebrating the Blessed Mawlid in the Maghrib.
